name: gfx_v12_0_rlc_resume
prose: Precondition: adev is an initialised amdgpu_device whose firmware load type and SR-IOV role are known and whose gfx.rlc.funcs stop/start callbacks are set. Behaviour: if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_PSP it initialises the clear-state buffer and, unless the device is an SR-IOV VF, enables the RLC SRM, then returns 0 without stopping or starting the RLC. For any other load type, an SR-IOV VF only initialises the clear-state buffer and returns 0; otherwise it stops the RLC, writes 0 to the RLC_CGCG_CGLS_CTRL (clock gating) and RLC_PG_CNTL (power gating) registers, loads the RLC microcode with gfx_v12_0_rlc_load_microcode only if the load type is AMDGPU_FW_LOAD_DIRECT, returning its error immediately on failure (that function returns -EINVAL when adev->gfx.rlc_fw is NULL or its header major version is not 2, in which case the RLC stays stopped with CG/PG disabled, the clear-state buffer not initialised and the RLC not started), then initialises the clear-state buffer, starts the RLC and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is gfx_v12_0.c:2070-2106 and gfx_v12_0_rlc_load_microcode (2042-2068). Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 RIGHT: a NULL rlc_fw is handled with -EINVAL, so a valid blob is not a precondition.

name: jpeg_v5_0_1_hw_start_sriov_placeholder
note: no function with this name exists in jpeg_v5_0_1.c; the listed prose is empty ('Precondition: none. Postcondition: none.') and there is nothing to describe; the real SR-IOV start function is jpeg_v5_0_1_start_sriov (line 449), outside this slice and not the listed item.

name: vcn_v3_0_stop
prose: Precondition: vinst points to a valid amdgpu_vcn_inst of an initialised amdgpu_device. Behaviour: it returns 0 at once, touching nothing, if the instance's bit is set in adev->vcn.harvest_config. If AMD_PG_SUPPORT_VCN_DPG is set in pg_flags it calls vcn_v3_0_stop_dpg_mode (which waits on status registers but ignores the wait results and returns 0) and goes to done with r = 0, skipping the VCPU reset and the clock/power-gating steps. Otherwise it waits for UVD_STATUS idle, for the LMI write/read-clean bits and, after stalling the UMC arbitration, for the UMC read/write-clean raw bits, going to done with the error of the first wait that fails. If all waits succeed it blocks VCPU register access, resets the VCPU, disables the VCPU clock, applies the LMI and LMI_UMC soft resets, clears UVD_STATUS, enables clock gating and static power gating, and falls into done. At done, if adev->pm.dpm_enabled it calls amdgpu_dpm_enable_vcn(adev, false, i) and then returns r (0 or the failed wait's error).
note: checked vcn_v3_0.c:1594-1711. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (a harvested instance returns before the dpm disable, lines 1639-1640); round 2 RIGHT (the DPG path always returns 0); the original claim (DPG path returns without VCPU reset) RIGHT.

name: vega10_ih_irq_init
prose: Precondition: adev is an initialised amdgpu_device whose IH rings adev->irq.ih, ih1 and ih2 have ring_size, doorbell and register offsets configured. Behaviour: it calls vega10_ih_toggle_interrupts(adev, false) and returns its error if nonzero; calls nbio.funcs->ih_control; on CHIP_RENOIR reads mmIH_CHICKEN, sets MC_SPACE_GPA_ENABLE if irq.ih.use_bus_addr is set and writes it back. For each of ih, ih1, ih2 whose ring_size is nonzero it calls vega10_ih_enable_ring and returns the first error immediately. Unless the device is an SR-IOV VF it calls nbio.funcs->ih_doorbell_range with irq.ih's use_doorbell and doorbell_index. It then calls pci_set_master, calls vega10_ih_toggle_interrupts(adev, true) and returns its error if nonzero, sets irq.ih_soft.enabled to true when irq.ih_soft.ring_size is nonzero, and returns 0. On an early error return the remaining steps are not performed.
note: slice cut head; function is vega10_ih.c:261-307 (the packet name vega10_ih_irq_enable does not exist). Old prose matches the code; the rings iterated are only ih, ih1 and ih2 (ih_soft is handled separately).

name: destroy_queue_cpsch
prose: Precondition: q belongs to qpd on dqm; the caller must hold q->process->mutex (wait_on_destroy_queue releases and re-takes it) and must not hold the dqm lock. Behaviour: for an SDMA or SDMA_XGMI queue it first reads the queue counter from user memory and only logs a failure (the counter then counts as 0). It takes the dqm lock and calls wait_on_destroy_queue, which returns -EBUSY (leaving q->properties.is_being_destroyed set) if the queue is already being destroyed, otherwise sets the flag and, if debug trap is enabled and the queue is suspended, waits interruptibly for it to resume (resetting the flag and returning the wait's error on interruption); it does nothing and returns 0 if the process device is missing or qpd is in debug mode. A nonzero return releases the dqm lock and is returned. If qpd->is_debug it resets is_being_destroyed to false and returns -EBUSY. Otherwise it deallocates the doorbell, for SDMA queues deallocates the sdma queue and adds the read counter to the process device's sdma_past_activity_counter, and, if the queue is active, decrements the queue count, clears is_active and runs execute_queues_cpsch (setting qpd->reset_wavefronts on -ETIME) or, with MES, remove_queue_mes; the result becomes the return value. It then unlinks the queue from qpd's list, decrements qpd->queue_count and dqm->total_queue_count, releases the dqm lock, raises the EC_DEVICE_QUEUE_DELETE debug event and frees the MQD, returning 0 for an inactive queue or the unmap/remove result (which can be a negative error even though the queue was removed and freed). is_being_destroyed stays true on those paths.
note: checked kfd_device_queue_manager.c:2561-2654 and wait_on_destroy_queue (2527-2559). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (mutex precondition); original reviewer RIGHT (error returned after the queue was removed).

name: kfd_signal_hw_exception_event
prose: Precondition: pasid is a PASID; the function may be called from workqueue context. Behaviour: it looks up the KFD process with kfd_lookup_process_by_pasid, which takes a reference on it; if there is none it returns. Otherwise it calls lookup_events_by_type_and_signal(p, KFD_EVENT_TYPE_HW_EXCEPTION, NULL) to signal the process's hardware-exception events and drops the process reference with kfd_unref_process. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut head; function is kfd_events.c:1195-1209 and matches the old prose. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG for this function: it does look up by pasid and call lookup_events_by_type_and_signal (lines 1202-1207); that description fits a different function in this file.

name: init_event_waiter
prose: Precondition: p, waiter and event_data are valid and the caller holds p->event_mutex. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL, without touching waiter, if lookup_event_by_id finds no event for event_data->event_id. Otherwise, under ev->lock, it sets waiter->event, sets waiter->activated to ev->signaled, clears ev->signaled if it was set and the event is not auto-reset, and, if the event is KFD_EVENT_TYPE_SIGNAL and event_data->signal_event_data.last_event_age is nonzero, sets waiter->event_age_enabled to true (even when the ages are equal) and sets waiter->activated to true if ev->event_age differs from last_event_age. If waiter->activated is false it adds the waiter to ev->wq. It releases ev->lock and returns 0.
note: kfd_events.c:841-868. Matches the old prose; reviewer round 2's note (age-enabled even when equal) is consistent with it.

name: kfd_wait_on_events
prose: Precondition: p is a kfd_process, data points to num_events user kfd_event_data entries, user_timeout_ms and wait_result are writable; the caller does not hold p->event_mutex. Behaviour: it converts the timeout, allocates the waiter array (-ENOMEM on failure, going to the exit that sets *wait_result to KFD_IOC_WAIT_RESULT_FAIL), takes p->event_mutex and for each event copies its data from user memory (-EFAULT on failure) and calls init_event_waiter (its -EINVAL for a bad id is returned); any such failure unlocks via out_unlock. It tests the wait condition once; if it is COMPLETE it copies the signalled event data back to user memory and returns that result (-EFAULT possible); if the test returns FAIL it WARNs and goes to out_unlock. Otherwise it drops the mutex and loops: a fatal signal gives -EINTR; any other pending signal gives -ERESTARTSYS and, unless the timeout was IMMEDIATE or INFINITE, updates *user_timeout_ms with the remaining time; otherwise it sleeps until the condition changes or the timeout expires. After the loop it retakes the mutex and, if there was no error and the result is COMPLETE, copies the signalled event data to user memory (an -EFAULT is returned). out_unlock frees the waiters (re-arming auto-reset events that were consumed only when the return value is -ERESTARTSYS) and releases the mutex. At the final exit it sets *wait_result to KFD_IOC_WAIT_RESULT_FAIL if ret is nonzero, and converts a FAIL result with ret 0 into -EIO. Success returns 0 with *wait_result COMPLETE or TIMEOUT.
note: kfd_events.c:981-1095. Matches the old prose; the free_waiters argument semantics (undo of auto-reset only for -ERESTARTSYS) were taken from the call at line 1086 without reading free_waiters.

name: dm_crtc_get_cursor_mode
prose: Precondition: state is the atomic state, dm_crtc_state the CRTC's amdgpu state, cursor_mode a writable pointer; zpos values are normalised. Behaviour: if the DCE hardware IP version is 4.0.1 (DCN401) it sets *cursor_mode to DM_CURSOR_NATIVE_MODE and returns 0. Otherwise it initialises *cursor_mode to dm_crtc_state->cursor_mode and scans the old/new plane states of planes on this CRTC; it records whether the cursor plane is in the state and stops with consider_mode_change set when a plane was enabled, disabled, changed format, or changed scale (it dereferences both old and new fb formats). If no plane changed and zpos did not change it returns 0 with *cursor_mode unchanged; if the cursor plane is not in the state and is not in the CRTC's plane mask it also returns 0. It gets the cursor plane state with drm_atomic_get_plane_state and returns its error pointer value if that fails (with *cursor_mode unchanged); if the cursor has no framebuffer it returns 0 unchanged. Then, for the other planes of this CRTC in descending z-order, it sets *cursor_mode to DM_CURSOR_OVERLAY_MODE and returns 0 as soon as a plane has a video format or has both its horizontal and vertical scale different from the cursor's, and stops scanning at the first plane that covers the whole CRTC. Finally it sets *cursor_mode to DM_CURSOR_NATIVE_MODE if a plane covered the entire CRTC and DM_CURSOR_OVERLAY_MODE otherwise, and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; real name is dm_crtc_get_cursor_mode(adev, state, dm_crtc_state, cursor_mode) (amdgpu_dm.c:12319-12441), not amdgpu_dm_crtc_compute_cursor_mode with a crtc_state parameter; the old prose checks out against the code except for its parameter list.

name: dm_crtc_high_irq_handler
prose: Precondition: adev and acrtc are valid; on DCN it is called from dm_vupdate_high_irq at VUPDATE_NO_LOCK and on DCE from dm_crtc_high_irq at VLINE0. Behaviour: if acrtc->wb_conn exists it clears wb_pending under the connector's job_lock when set and, if a writeback job was queued, waits one frame period with mdelay, signals the writeback completion with status 0 and force-disables writeback on the stream. It runs amdgpu_dm_crtc_handle_vblank only if the ASIC is DCN or VRR is inactive, and always runs the CRC irq handler. If adev->family is older than AMDGPU_FAMILY_AI it returns there. Otherwise, with the DRM event lock held (irqsave): when the CRTC has a stream whose vrr_params.supported is set it calls mod_freesync_handle_v_update and, if freesync is in VRR_STATE_ACTIVE_VARIABLE or neither PSR nor Replay is enabled, queues schedule_dc_vmin_vmax (which retains the stream and queues a worker that applies the adjust under dc_lock, releases the stream and frees its allocations; it silently does nothing if its allocations fail). On DCN, a flip with pflip_status AMDGPU_FLIP_SUBMITTED and a pending event is completed (event sent, vblank reference dropped, status set to AMDGPU_FLIP_NONE) when dc_get_flip_pending_on_otg reports no pending flip, otherwise it stays armed; on DCN, a SUBMITTED flip without a pending event and with no active planes is reset to AMDGPU_FLIP_NONE without sending an event or dropping a vblank reference. It then releases the event lock.
note: checked amdgpu_dm.c:590-712 and schedule_dc_vmin_vmax (550-576). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (the stream is retained by schedule_dc_vmin_vmax and released by the worker); round 2 RIGHT (the no-active-planes branch has no event); original RIGHT (the DCE path is driven by VLINE0).

name: amdgpu_dm_update_plane_color_mgmt
prose: Precondition: crtc is the dm_crtc_state, plane_state the DRM plane state and dc_plane_state the DC plane state being updated. Behaviour: it first calls amdgpu_dm_verify_lut3d_size and returns its error if nonzero. It takes the color capabilities from dc_plane_state->ctx->dc when available, sets the plane's input transfer function to bypass/linear, and calls __set_dm_plane_degamma: -ENOMEM is returned at once; if the CRTC has degamma (cm_has_degamma or cm_is_degamma_srgb) and that call did not return -EINVAL it returns -EINVAL (plane and CRTC degamma cannot both be used); if the CRTC has degamma it returns the error of map_crtc_degamma_to_dc_plane if that fails; any other nonzero result of __set_dm_plane_degamma is otherwise ignored. It then sets the gamut remap matrix from the plane CTM with enable_remap true when dm_plane_state->ctm is set, or sets enable_remap false, clears input_csc_color_matrix.enable_adjustment in both cases, and returns the result of amdgpu_dm_plane_set_color_properties.
note: slice cut head; real name amdgpu_dm_update_plane_color_mgmt (amdgpu_dm_color.c:1256-1340), no dm_plane_color_setup. Old prose omitted the amdgpu_dm_verify_lut3d_size early return.

name: amdgpu_dm_crtc_set_crc_source
prose: Precondition: crtc and src_name are valid. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if src_name does not parse to a known source (no lock taken), then takes the CRTC mutex with drm_modeset_lock and returns its error if that fails (lock not held). It takes a reference on the first pending CRTC commit, if any, and waits for its hw_done interruptibly with a 10 second timeout: a negative result or -ETIMEDOUT (timeout) goes to cleanup. For a DPRX source, or for source NONE when the current source is DPRX, it finds the first non-writeback connector bound to the CRTC and returns -EINVAL (via cleanup) if there is none, no aux, or the connector is not DisplayPort/eDP. If the CRC source goes from invalid to valid it calls drm_crtc_vblank_get (a nonzero result goes to cleanup and becomes the return value, overwriting any earlier value). It then calls amdgpu_dm_crtc_configure_crc_source (-EINVAL via cleanup on failure, the vblank reference taken earlier not dropped). When enabling a DPRX source it starts DP CRC (-EINVAL via cleanup on failure); when disabling it drops the vblank reference and stops DP CRC for a DPRX source (-EINVAL via cleanup if that fails, after the vblank reference was dropped). On success it stores the new source in acrtc->dm_irq_params.crc_src under the event lock, clears crc_skip_count and falls into cleanup. cleanup drops the commit reference if one was taken, unlocks the CRTC mutex and returns ret: 0 normally, but a positive remaining-jiffies value when a commit wait succeeded and no vblank_get overwrote it. crc_src is unchanged on every failure path.
note: checked amdgpu_dm_crc.c:562-738. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (the return after a successful wait is the positive jiffies value unless drm_crtc_vblank_get ran and reset ret to 0); round 2 RIGHT (early parse and lock-failure returns do not unlock); original RIGHT (vblank reference not dropped after a failed configure/start).

name: amdgpu_dm_plane_get_plane_formats
prose: Precondition: plane is an initialised drm_plane, formats has room for max_formats entries plus up to six more, plane_cap may be NULL. Behaviour: for a primary plane, or a non-cursor plane whose plane_cap type is DC_PLANE_TYPE_DCN_UNIVERSAL, it copies the rgb_formats table entries one by one, stopping once num_formats reaches max_formats, and then, without any bound check, appends DRM_FORMAT_NV12 if plane_cap->pixel_format_support.nv12, DRM_FORMAT_P010 if .p010, and four fp16 formats if .fp16, so the count can exceed max_formats by up to six. Otherwise an overlay plane copies overlay_formats and a cursor plane copies cursor_formats, each bounded by max_formats, and any other plane type writes nothing. It returns the number of formats written, takes no locks and keeps no references.
note: slice cut head; real name amdgpu_dm_plane_get_plane_formats(plane, plane_cap, formats, max_formats) (amdgpu_dm_plane.c:761-818). Old prose otherwise matches.

name: amdgpu_dm_psr_wait_disable
prose: Precondition: stream points to a valid dc_stream_state (stream->link is read). Behaviour: it returns false if stream->link is NULL. Otherwise it polls dc_link_get_psr_state up to 1001 times (retry_count 0 to 1000), stopping at the first poll that leaves psr_state equal to PSR_STATE0 and delaying 500 microseconds between polls that do not. It returns false if the loop ended with retry_count == 1000, that is PSR_STATE0 first seen on the poll with retry_count 1000, and true otherwise, which includes PSR_STATE0 seen on any earlier poll and also the case where it was never seen (the loop then ends with retry_count 1001). psr_state starts as PSR_STATE0.
note: slice cut head; function is amdgpu_dm_psr_wait_disable(stream) (amdgpu_dm_psr.c:257-277), taking a stream rather than a link. Old prose's logic is right; the 'never seen -> true' behaviour follows from the exit value 1001.

name: dc_clk_mgr_create
prose: Precondition: ctx->asic_id.chip_family selects the chip family; pp_smu and dccg are passed to the family constructors that use them. Behaviour: it switches on the chip family; for each handled family it kzallocs the family-specific clk_mgr object (BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER and return NULL if that fails), calls the constructor selected by family, revision or dce_version (DCE, DCN2 through DCN4 families) and returns a pointer to the embedded struct clk_mgr base. For FAMILY_VI and FAMILY_RV the object is returned even when no revision check matches, in which case no constructor ran and the object stays zeroed; for FAMILY_VGH only the Van Gogh revision is handled and others fall to the end. For AMDGPU_FAMILY_GC_12_0_0 the object is allocated by dcn401_clk_mgr_construct (NULL gives BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER and NULL). For an unhandled family, or a family handled only for some revisions that does not match, it hits ASSERT(0) (unknown family) or falls out of the switch and returns NULL. The caller owns the returned object and releases it with dc_destroy_clk_mgr.
note: slice cut head; real name dc_clk_mgr_create (clk_mgr.c:147-384). Old prose said that every non-matching revision returns NULL; FAMILY_VI and FAMILY_RV return the zeroed object (lines 207, 249) and only the default and FAMILY_VGH non-Van Gogh case reach NULL/ASSERT.

name: rn_update_clocks
prose: Precondition: clk_mgr_base is a valid clk_mgr, context holds the requested clocks in context->bw_ctx.bw.dcn.clk. Behaviour: it returns immediately if dc->work_arounds.skip_clock_update is set. If safe_to_lower is true and 48 MHz power-down is not disabled it sets the DCN power state to LOW_POWER (through the vbios SMU) only if the state is not already LOW_POWER and rn_get_active_display_cnt_wa is 0, and otherwise leaves it; if safe_to_lower is false or 48 MHz power-down is disabled it sets MISSION_MODE if the state is not already that. It programs dcfclk and the deep-sleep dcfclk through the SMU when should_set_clock allows. It then writes into the context's requested values: a nonzero requested dppclk below 100000 kHz is raised to 100000, and if either the requested dppclk or dispclk is 0 both are replaced by the current clocks. If should_set_clock allows it records the new dppclk (noting whether it was lowered) and dispclk, setting the dispclk through the SMU. When dppclk was lowered it updates the per-DPP DTOs with the requested dppclk, sets the dppclk through the SMU and updates the DTOs again with the actual dppclk; otherwise it sets the dppclk through the SMU if either dppclk or dispclk was updated and then updates the DTOs with the actual dppclk. If dispclk was updated and a dmcu exists and is initialised it sets the PSR wait loop count to dispclk / 1000 / 7. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut head; function is rn_clk_mgr.c:131-251. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (dppclk is also programmed when dispclk changes, lines 233-235); round 2 RIGHT (no state change when safe_to_lower with 48 MHz power-down enabled and displays still active); original RIGHT (early return on skip_clock_update).

name: dcn401_clk_mgr_construct
prose: Precondition: ctx and dccg are valid. Behaviour: this is the function dcn401_clk_mgr_construct; it kzallocs the dcn401_clk_mgr itself and returns NULL if that fails. It fills in the base clk_mgr (ctx, dcn401_funcs, register/shift/mask tables, dccg), dfs_bypass_disp_clk 0, dprefclk_ss_percentage 0, dprefclk_ss_divider 1000, ss_on_dprefclk false, dfs_ref_freq_khz 100000, dprefclk_khz 720000 and dentist_vco_freq_khz from the VCO register (4500000 when the register gives 0). It dumps the boot clock snapshot, sets clks.ref_dtbclk_khz to the snapshot dtbclk if debug.disable_dtb_ref_clk_switch is set and they differ, replaces dprefclk_khz with the snapshot dprefclk when that is nonzero, reads the spread-spectrum info, sets dfs_bypass_enabled and smu_present false, kzallocs bw_params (BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER, free the object and return NULL on failure) and allocates the watermark range table as GART memory with dm_helpers_allocate_gpu_mem (BREAK_TO_DEBUGGER, free bw_params and the object and return NULL on failure). It returns &clk_mgr401->base.
note: slice cut head; function is dcn401_clk_mgr.c:1547-1621. Old prose wrongly said the memory was already allocated by the caller (it is allocated at line 1552) and omitted the NULL return for that allocation.

name: update_planes_and_stream_state
prose: Precondition: dc, stream and the output pointers are valid, srf_updates has surface_count entries with non-NULL surfaces, stream_update may be NULL. Behaviour: it returns false (ASSERT only if surface_count is nonzero) without writing outputs if dc_stream_get_status(stream) is NULL. It computes the update type, forces immediate-flip planes to flip, and for a FULL update backs up the current plane and stream state into dc->scratch.current_state. It applies the stream update, and returns false (stream state already modified) if any surface update has a surface with a zero src or dst rect width or height and no scaling_info, or a scaling_info that has any zero src or dst dimension. It copies each surface update into its plane. For an update type of FULL it creates a copy of dc->current_state (returning false if that fails), removes phantom streams and planes, removes and re-adds all planes of the stream, and jumps to a failure label that releases the new context and returns false if either step fails. For MED updates with position changes it rebuilds scaling parameters. For a FULL update it validates bandwidth and returns false (releasing the new context) unless it returns DC_OK. It then updates seamless-boot flags, sets *new_context (the new copy for FULL, dc->current_state otherwise) and *new_update_type, and for a FULL update backs up the post-update state into dc->scratch.new_state, returning true.
note: slice cut head; function is dc.c:3451-3585. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (pre-update backup is done only when update_type is FULL, line 3481-3482); round 2 RIGHT (any zero dimension in scaling_info fails).

name: vpg3_construct
prose: Precondition: vpg3 points to storage for a dcn30_vpg owned by the caller; ctx, inst and the register, shift and mask tables are valid. Behaviour: it allocates nothing and returns nothing; it sets vpg3->base.ctx to ctx, base.inst to inst, base.funcs to &dcn30_vpg_funcs, and the regs, vpg_shift and vpg_mask pointers to the given tables.
note: slice cut head; real function is vpg3_construct (dcn30_vpg.c:249-264), a void constructor; the old prose described a non-existent allocating function.

name: CalculateVMAndRowBytes
prose: Precondition: mode_lib->vba.GPUVMMaxPageTableLevels is initialised, BytePerPixel, VMMPageSize and Pitch are nonzero where they are divisors, and the output pointers are valid. Behaviour: a pure computation that returns PDEAndMetaPTEBytesFrame, the sum of MetaPTEBytesFrame, MPDEBytesFrame, DPDE0BytesFrame and ExtraDPDEBytesFrame. When DCCEnable it computes *meta_row_height and *MetaRowByte from the scan direction and SwathWidth and, with GPUVMEnable, MetaPTEBytesFrame and MPDEBytesFrame; when DCC is off they are 0 and *MetaRowByte is 0. It picks the macro tile size and height from SurfaceTiling and stores *MacroTileWidth. DPDE0BytesFrame and ExtraDPDEBytesFrame are nonzero only when GPUVMEnable and GPUVMMaxPageTableLevels > 1. If GPUVMEnable it computes the PTE request geometry from the tiling, then *dpte_row_height and *PixelPTEBytesPerRow for the linear, horizontal-scan or vertical-scan case, and sets *PTEBufferSizeNotExceeded to whether *PixelPTEBytesPerRow * (1 - FractionOfPTEReturnDrop) <= 64 * PTEBufferSizeInRequestsLuma; if GPUVMEnable is false it sets *PixelPTEBytesPerRow to 0, *PTEBufferSizeNotExceeded to true and leaves *dpte_row_height unchanged.
note: slice cut head; the real function is CalculateVMAndRowBytes in display_mode_vba_20.c:856-1080 (no dml20_pte_row_calc exists). Read in full.

name: CalculateWatermarksAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport
prose: Precondition: the per-plane arrays have NumberOfActivePlanes valid entries and the output pointers are valid; *UrgentWatermark is written before it is read. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It sets *UrgentWatermark = UrgentLatency + ExtraLatency, *DRAMClockChangeWatermark = DRAMClockChangeLatency + *UrgentWatermark, and the writeback watermarks from WritebackLatency (adding a chunk-size term when more than one writeback is active). It computes, for each plane, the effective line-buffer hiding, the DET buffering times, the active DRAM-clock-change latency margin (reduced for multiple planes, combined with chroma and writeback margins) and stores them in mode_lib->vba (TotalActiveDPP, TotalDCCActiveDPP, TotalActiveWriteback, TotalNumberOfActiveOTG, ActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencyMargin, MinActiveDRAMClockChangeMargin and the intermediate line-buffer fields). It sets *MinActiveDRAMClockChangeLatencySupported = MinActiveDRAMClockChangeMargin + DRAMClockChangeLatency; *DRAMClockChangeSupport to dm_dram_clock_change_vactive if the minimum margin is positive, else dm_dram_clock_change_vblank if PrefetchMode is 0 and (SynchronizedVBlank, exactly one OTG, or a positive second-smallest margin), else dm_dram_clock_change_unsupported. It finds the stutter-critical plane (smallest full DET buffering time) and sets *StutterExitWatermark = SRExitTime + ExtraLatency + 10 / DCFCLKDeepSleep and *StutterEnterPlusExitWatermark to the maximum of SREnterPlusExitTime + ExtraLatency + 10 / DCFCLKDeepSleep and that plane's time to finish the swath transfer.
note: slice cut head; real function is CalculateWatermarksAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport (display_mode_vba_30.c:5067-5282). Checked outputs at lines 5153-5176, 5237-5282; divisions by plane quantities are unguarded.

name: CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Precondition: mode_lib->vba is initialised and the pipe, byte counts and output pointers are valid; myPipe->HTotal, PixelClock and the clocks used as divisors are nonzero. Behaviour: the return value is an error flag (true means failure, false means the schedule validated). name: DISPCLKDPPCLKDCFCLKDeepSleepPrefetchParametersWatermarksAndPerformanceCalculation

The loop ends when PrefetchAndImmediateFlipSupported is true or VStartupLines exceeds MaximumMaxVStartupLines (so after the loop it can still be false, which only triggers ASSERT(v->PrefetchAndImmediateFlipSupported)); afterwards the function computes the unbounded request and compressed buffer size and calls CalculateWatermarksAndDRAMSpeedChangeSupport. name: TruncToValidBPP
prose: Precondition: PixelClock is nonzero; HTotal, HActive, DSCSlices, AudioRate and AudioLayout are not used. Behaviour: a pure function returning a bits-per-pixel value as a double, or BPP_INVALID. From Format it selects the non-DSC tiers and DSC limits: for dm_420 the non-DSC values 12, 15, 18 with MinDSCBPP 6 and MaxDSCBPP 1.5 * DSCInputBitPerComponent - 1/16; for dm_444 24, 30, 36 with 8 and 3 * bpc - 1/16; otherwise 16, 20, 24 with MinDSCBPP 7 and MaxDSCBPP 2 * bpc - 1/16 for dm_n422 or 8 and 3 * bpc - 1/16 for the other formats. MaxLinkBPP is LinkBitRate / 10 * 8 * Lanes / PixelClock, multiplied by (1 - 2.4/100) when DSCEnable and Output is dm_dp, then capped at 16 for dm_odm_combine_mode_4to1 or at 32 for dm_odm_combine_mode_2to1 if it is larger. If DesiredBPP is 0: with DSC it returns BPP_INVALID if MaxLinkBPP < MinDSCBPP, MaxDSCBPP if MaxLinkBPP >= MaxDSCBPP, else floor(16 * MaxLinkBPP) / 16; without DSC it returns the third tier if MaxLinkBPP >= it, else the second tier if MaxLinkBPP >= it, else 16.0 if MaxLinkBPP >= the first tier, otherwise BPP_INVALID. If DesiredBPP is nonzero it returns DesiredBPP when (no DSC and DesiredBPP equals the third or second tier or is at most the first tier) or (DSC and MinDSCBPP <= DesiredBPP <= MaxDSCBPP), and BPP_INVALID otherwise.

name: CalculateStutterEfficiency
prose: Precondition: the per-plane arrays have NumberOfActivePlanes entries and all output pointers are valid; TotalDataReadBandwidth, TotalCompressedReadBandwidth, ReturnBW, DCFCLK, PixelClock[k], SwathWidthY[k], BytePerPixelDETY[k], VRatio[k] and the resulting *StutterPeriod must be nonzero or the divisions are undefined; with no active planes *StutterPeriod is not assigned by this function. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It sums the compressed, zero-size and row read bandwidths (applying a DCC maximum effective compression of 2 or 4 per plane), derives the average DCC compression rate and zero-size fraction and the EffectiveCompressedBufferSize. For each plane it computes LinesInDETY and the DET buffering time, and sets *StutterPeriod to the smallest such time (the first plane always sets it), recording that plane's frame and active times, swath data and MinTTUVBlank as the critical plane. It computes StutterBurstTime (raised to at least the time to finish the critical swath), counts active writebacks, and, if none, sets *StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank and *Z8StutterEfficiencyNotIncludingVBlank to max(0, 1 - (SRExitTime or SRExitZ8Time + StutterBurstTime) / *StutterPeriod) * 100 and both burst counts to ceil(VActiveTimeCriticalPlane / *StutterPeriod) when the corresponding efficiency is above 0 (otherwise 0); with a writeback active all four are 0. It then counts OTGs (planes with BlendingAndTiming[k] == k) and sets *StutterEfficiency (and the Z8 value) to 0 when the not-including-VBlank efficiency is not above 0, to the formula 1 - (bursts * SRExitTime + StutterBurstTime * VActiveTime / StutterPeriod) / FrameTime (times 100) when (SynchronizedVBlank or one OTG) and LastStutterPeriod + MinTTUVBlankCriticalPlane exceeds the stutter enter-plus-exit watermark, and otherwise to the not-including-VBlank value; the Z8 case uses *NumberOfStutterBurstsPerFrame (not the Z8 count) in its last-period and efficiency formulas.
note: slice cut head; function is display_mode_vba_314.c:6389-6705. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (*StutterPeriod is used as a divisor); the old claim '*StutterPeriod is 0 when there are no active planes' is wrong: with no planes the loop does not assign it.

name: dml32_CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Precondition: v and myPipe describe a valid pipe, all output pointers are valid, LineTime inputs are nonzero. Behaviour: the return value is an error flag (true means failure). It computes the dynamic-metadata, VUpdate and setup parameters, then returns true immediately if myPipe->Dppclk or myPipe->Dispclk is 0, before writing *DSTXAfterScaler and the prefetch results. Otherwise it computes *DSTXAfterScaler, *DSTYAfterScaler and *Tno_bw and the one-to-one and equation prefetch schedules. When using the equation schedule it sets MyError instead of choosing it if ExtendPrefetchIfPossible is set, TPreReq is 0 and VStartup < MaxVStartup (so the caller can retry with a larger VStartup); it then sets *DestinationLinesForPrefetch, *PrefetchBandwidth, the VM and row request lines, *VRatioPrefetchY/C (setting MyError and 0 when the swath constraints fail) and *RequiredPrefetchPixDataBWLuma/Chroma when LinesToRequestPrefetchPixelData >= 1 and prefetch_bw_equ > 0, and sets MyError otherwise. It computes *prefetch_vmrow_bw, setting MyError if a needed request-lines value is not positive; if MyError it zeroes *PrefetchBandwidth, the two request-lines outputs, *DestinationLinesForPrefetch, the VRatio outputs and the required pixel-data bandwidths, and it returns MyError.

name: dml32_CalculateStutterEfficiency
prose: Precondition: the per-surface arrays have NumberOfActiveSurfaces entries and all output pointers are valid; TotalDataReadBandwidth, the compressed-bandwidth totals, ReturnBW, DCFCLK and *StutterPeriod must be nonzero where they are divisors, and with no non-phantom surface *StutterPeriod is not assigned. Behaviour: it returns nothing. Surfaces using MALL phantom pipes are skipped everywhere. It computes the compression-based EffectiveCompressedBufferSize like the dcn314 version, then for each non-phantom surface the DET buffering time and sets *StutterPeriod to the smallest of them (the first one found always sets it), recording that critical surface's frame/active times, swath data, DET size and MinTTUVBlank, and whether it is single-plane and single-pipe. StutterBurstTime is the larger of the computed burst time and the time to finish the critical swath. With no active writeback it sets the stutter and Z8 efficiencies not including vblank to max(0, 1 - (SRExitTime or SRExitZ8Time + StutterBurstTime) / *StutterPeriod) * 100 and the burst counts to ceil(VActiveTimeCriticalSurface / *StutterPeriod) when positive, otherwise all four are 0. It counts OTGs and checks that all of them have the same timing, and sets *StutterEfficiency and *Z8StutterEfficiency as in the dcn314 version except that the vblank-inclusive formula also requires SameTiming. Finally it sets *DCHUBBUB_ARB_CSTATE_MAX_CAP_MODE to false only when unbounded requests are disabled, there is exactly one surface that is single-plane and single-pipe, the last swath chunk size is in 1..4096 and the missing part of the last DET swath is in 1..the last chunk size, and to true otherwise.
note: slice cut head; real name dml32_CalculateStutterEfficiency (display_mode_vba_util_32.c:5587-6060); the packet's unnamed-fragment description only covered the compression and period part.

name: dml32_rq_dlg_get_dlg_reg
prose: Precondition: mode_lib, e2e_pipe_param, num_pipes and pipe_idx describe a valid configuration with pipe_idx < num_pipes, and dlg_regs and ttu_regs are writable; the pixel clock used for ref_freq_to_pix_freq is nonzero. Behaviour: it returns nothing and starts by zeroing both *dlg_regs and *ttu_regs. It converts timing and prefetch values obtained from the VBA getters (min_ttu_vblank, min_dst_y_next_start, vready, dst_x/y_after_scaler, dst_y_prefetch and the vm/row vblank and flip line counts, line and request delivery times, pte-group and meta-chunk times) into fixed-point dlg and ttu register fields. refcyc_h_blank_end is written only when ODM combine is disabled, 2to1 or 4to1; refcyc_per_vm_dmdata only when dynamic metadata and GPUVM are enabled; the chroma delivery values only for a dual-plane format; the cursor request times only if the source has a cursor. It also fills the ttu_regs fields (request delivery times, QoS levels, min_ttu_vblank), clamps the VM group/request and PTE-group/meta-chunk reference-cycle fields to 2^23 - 1 when they reach 2^23, and uses ASSERT to check ranges (ref_freq_to_pix_freq < 4, refcyc_h_blank_end < 2^13, the vm/row-per-vblank limits, dst_y_prefetch > the sum of the vm and row lines, at most one cursor, min_dst_y_next_start < 2^18, and several 13/17-bit field limits). It then prints the regs and returns.

name: dcn35_populate_dml_pipes_from_context_fpu
prose: Precondition: dc, context and pipes are valid, pipes has room for dc->res_pool->pipe_count entries, and FPU access is enabled (it calls dc_assert_fp_enabled); validate_mode is the DC validation mode passed on to dcn31. Behaviour: it calls dcn31_populate_dml_pipes_from_context and then, for each pipe in context->res_ctx with a stream, sets pipes[pipe_cnt].pipe.dest.vtotal to adjust.v_total_min only when adjust.v_total_max equals v_total_min and v_total_min exceeds timing->v_total; sets dest.vblank_nom to timing->v_total - dest.vactive, then applies min(num_lines), max(v_sync_width + v_back_porch + 2) and finally min(1023), so the final value is at most 1023 and exceeds num_lines whenever the lower bound is larger than num_lines (and when the lower bound exceeds 1023 the result is 1023, below that bound); sets src.immediate_flip to true, src.unbounded_req_mode to false, zeroes the DCC fraction via dcn31_zero_pipe_dcc_fraction, sets dest.vfront_porch, src.dcc_rate to 3, dout.dsc_input_bpc (0, or 8/10/12 when dout.dsc_enable is set, with ASSERT(0) on another depth) and src.gpuvm_min_page_size_kbytes to 256; records an upscaling plane; and increments pipe_cnt. It then sets det_buffer_size_kbytes to 384 and dc->config.enable_4to1MPC to false; if exactly one pipe was populated (using the last pipe seen), it has a plane and z9_mpc is not disabled, it enables 4to1MPC for a dual-plane format with source at most 1920x1080 or, for a non-dual-plane format with source width at most 5120, sets det_buffer_size_kbytes to 192 and pipes[0].src.unbounded_req_mode to true; otherwise it uses crb_alloc_policy * 64 for det_buffer_size_kbytes when stream_count reaches crb_alloc_policy_min_disp_count and the policy exceeds DET_SIZE_DEFAULT, or 192 when there are at least 3 streams and an upscaled plane. Finally it scans the pipes and, for the first eDP stream with seamless_boot_odm_combine, apply_seamless_boot_optimization and apply_boot_odm_mode equal to dm_odm_combine_policy_2to1, sets vba.ODMCombinePolicy to dm_odm_combine_policy_2to1 and stops scanning. It returns pipe_cnt, the number of pipes with a stream.

name: CalculatePrefetchSchedule
prose: Precondition: scratch and p are valid; p holds the pipe description, byte counts, flags and output pointers and scratch holds the locals structure. Behaviour: the return value is an error flag (true means failure). It starts with s->MyError false, computes the host-VM trip levels and the dynamic-metadata and VUpdate parameters (writing the Tdmdl, Tdmdl_vm and NotEnoughTimeForDynamicMetadata outputs), and returns true immediately if p->myPipe->Dppclk or Dispclk is 0, before writing the DST after-scaler outputs and prefetch results. Otherwise it computes the after-scaler position, Tno_bw and the one-to-one and equation prefetch schedules and fills the prefetch outputs (lines for prefetch, prefetch bandwidth, vm and row request lines, prefetch VRatios and required prefetch pixel data bandwidths), setting s->MyError when the schedule is infeasible. It computes *p->prefetch_vmrow_bw and sets MyError if a needed request-lines value is not positive. On error it zeroes the request-lines outputs, *DestinationLinesForPrefetch, the VRatio outputs and the two required prefetch bandwidths (this variant does not zero *PrefetchBandwidth), and it returns s->MyError.
